column1: # PROPOSED rows for 0_Brain/learnings/_rules_index.tsv. NOT APPLIED. Columns 1-7 are the index's own; column 8 is the reason. Tuesday claims the index before applying any of them.

column7: When Kam answers a card with a note, not an option: the note IS the ruling and may be wider than the options. Record it verbatim by hand (the reconciler cannot parse a note) and state my reading back in the same action, naming what I treat as still his.
column8: CHANGE seats wednesday,friday -> all (rule text unchanged). The rule is about how any seat reads a card answered with a note; nothing in it is Secuura-only (the lesson's 'How to apply' 1-2 are general). Tuesday posts and rules cards daily. Row #2 of the same lesson (the KS-1175 hold itself) stays wednesday,friday.

column7: When a card or brief would open any field to the public: state what the field HOLDS (the column and how the write side fills it), never just its name. A field named OrganizationId held a user id and Kam ruled on the wrong description.
column8: CHANGE seats wednesday,friday -> all (rule text unchanged). A card-writing rule with no client content; Friday's own replay (row 32) noted it was absent from the card moment list. Rows plain, #3 and #4 of this lesson are Secuura product rulings and stay as they are.

column7: Before a kit, commit text or PR body says who decided ('product owner', 'ruling', 'Kam'): grep those words, run decision_queue.sh show <id>, check the card's client_project and option detail name THIS lane. A decision I made is written as mine.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-17 (B1675) and 2026-11-18 (B1695, w=2, diagnosis mandatory): a ruling was attributed to Kam in a stamped kit twice in two days; the second time the card existed but named another project. Existing rule 3 says 'find the card'; the seat found it and still got the scope wrong, because kam_rulings_today prints only the option key and label. The rule exists only in the ledger row. NOTE: the lesson file does not hold this text; the lesson needs a dated section added in the same action (see REPORT gap G1).

column7: Before stamping a kit READ WHOLE: read it with the Read tool, or print the tail of every line a display cut; never through cut -c. Each frozen sentence saying what code, a test or a gate finding DOES gets its source lines printed in the stamp action.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-15 s279 (kit read through cut -c1-1200, 8 long lines cut), s275 B1552 and B1553 (w=2: drafter's characterisation of a finding / of a test stamped unread). The card's only cut -c line (false-absence rule 2) is about absence claims in mail, a different moment. Ledger-only today.

column7: After every stamp, before launch: print the kit's byte count and last line and check them against the kit's own Step-0 rule; a stamp tool's OK proves slots are filled, not their shape. Rewrite a kit via temp file then os.replace, never open(path,'w') first.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-16 s283 (kit left at 0 bytes, stamp_check rc 0 on empty) and 2026-11-17 s286 (READ-WHOLE label doubled, stamp_brief printed OK). Both caught by eye; the mechanism built covers the empty kit only. Ledger-only today.

column7: When a kit changes an answer the code gives (status, gate) or tells a seat to MATCH a tool's output: quote the output from a real run, list each step's inputs against the step that makes them, and carry a by-program census of tests pinning the OLD answer.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-12 s274 B1545 (w=3 REGRESSION: expected output wording and step order frozen unrun) and 2026-11-15 s275 B1555 (seat stopped three times on the kit's own expectations). Rule 4 covers command literals and predicted figures, not expected OUTPUT strings, step dependencies or the census. stamp_check.py is a hard gate in tuesday/brief_seat.sh but measures a literal's presence, not its sense (ledger 2026-11-18 s288), so enforced_by stays '-'.

column7: Before a card that removes or retires an environment, deliverable or named artefact of a client project: grep the signed contract (SOW) for it and state the hits on the card, or write 'SOW not read'. A removal ruled on a missing premise cannot be undone.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-06 s245/s247 (w=10 REGRESSION, the one row in Friday's replay with an IRREVERSIBLE cost: a demo the signed SOW names was carded for removal and deleted). Friday's replay graded it LEDGER-ONLY (row 83) and said it 'does not fit' rule 1; the index still has 0 hits for SOW or contract. It fits as its own row.

column7: Before commissioning a lane from a sweep or census: grep the pickup and today's note for the lane id and ticket keys and read every DROPPED or HELD line; a sweep is dated the hour it ran. A hold Kam set is lifted only by his word naming it.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-15 s278 (drafter commissioned for a lane dropped that morning under Kam's Guided hold) and 2026-11-16 s281 (a 'pending' from a PR body relayed to Kam as current). The card has the general 'a re-recon is dated' clause inside a triage rule; nothing at the commission moment.

column7: Before a head-pinned merge: read the printed check TABLE and confirm it names every job that repo expects (tuesday/tools/pr_checks_wait.sh --min-checks N, N from the last merged PR); never merge on the ALL GREEN line. A finished set of 1 is not the set.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-18 s287 (ALL GREEN printed one second after the PR opened, on 1 of 7 checks). '--at merge' prints 7 rules for this seat and none mentions the check set. The tool now refuses a repo with no expected count, but a merge can be made without the tool, so enforced_by stays '-' (spec: a tool that can be bypassed is a rule).

column7: Before calling a scheduled output missing or late: print its due time converted to local time (date -j) beside the current time in the same command and require now > due plus a grace period. Before the due time an absence is not an absence.
column8: NEW row. Tuesday ledger 2026-11-13 s274 (told Kam a digest was missing two hours before it was due; UTC and AEDT compared by eye; two cards and an investigation seat spent). The card's clock line gives the UTC offset but no rule at the 'missing' claim.
